key_insight: Large language models can drive a search-and-evaluate loop to synthesize instance-optimal, workload- and hardware-specialized heuristics automatically, replacing brittle hand-designed rules with per-instance high-performance policies.
problem_solved: Designing and continuously tuning resource-management heuristics (scheduling, caching, AQM, etc.) is costly and brittle as hardware, workloads, and environments change; the paper automates creation of heuristics tailored to each instance.
method: Use an LLM to generate candidate heuristic implementations (pseudo-code or code) conditioned on workload and hardware characteristics.
Evaluate candidates with a performance-guided search loop (simulate or measure on-target), use results to refine prompts / selection, and iterate to converge on instance-optimal heuristics.
Compile/validate the selected heuristic and deploy it to the system, optionally with fallback/safety checks.
impact: Practitioners get automated, per-instance tuned policies that improve resource utilization and performance while cutting developer effort and time-to-deploy for system-level optimizations.

paper_title: Vulcan: Instance-Optimal Systems Heuristics Through LLM-Driven Search
paper_authors: Rohit Dwivedula, Divyanshu Saxena, Sujay Yadalam, Daehyeok Kim, Aditya Akella
